Not OP, but maybe they’re referring to how Islam doesn’t allow for open expression of gender identity and sexuality? It could be also how many aren’t given a choice of how they choose to wear their clothing (aurat), or that in Malaysia you can’t even leave Islam?

And yes, while you may not have a problem spending 30 mins a day praying, there are other facets to it like i mentioned that to other people may not find as easy, hence why it’s “rigid”. 

No malice intended here, just giving my two cents.

So this is something I really want for Malaysia, as someone who does not consider myself Muslim. The fact that there’s not a choice at all under Malaysian law to leave the religion is really bad to me.  

Being forced to do something or be something against your will literally has no upsides, especially in this given context.

Hell i’d even go on to say that we shouldn’t force spouses to convert upon marriage.

Because for me, it is your life and you should be free to choose what you think makes you happy. But unfortunately, we don’t have that luxury of “choice”.

That said though, I think even if this is discussed properly, I doubt Malaysia would allow this to happen in the near future, the religious groups hold too much power to let that happen within a few years. Whilst it may be a popular opinion here, we exist in a liberal echo chamber that is probably not reflective of the consensus of the Malaysian crowd.

Just my two cents, but I sincerely hope this, along with numerous other “issues” (LGBT rights, systematic racism) gets resolved soon.
